phase1_assignment.objective: Audit generic scientist-agent evidence packaging, reproducibility and handoff mechanisms that preserve observation/inference/uncertainty and exact continuation.

observations.mechanism: validation-derived failure memory has a matched scientist-agent ablation benefit, but retrieval relevance is still only semantic similarity rather than target-side mechanism revalidation
observations.evidence: EvoScientist stores unsuccessful idea directions identified by Idea Validation Evolution (IVE) and later retrieves ideation-memory items by top-k embedding cosine similarity. In its matched ablation, removing IVE makes the variant lose to full EvoScientist on feasibility in 63.33% of pairwise comparisons. This directly supports recording validation-derived failed directions as reusable memory, while the published retrieval mechanism does not itself check mechanism/assumption compatibility or run a bounded target-side probe before reuse.
observations.scope: Computational AI-scientist idea generation. The 63.33% result isolates IVE within EvoScientist, not the stronger target-side revalidation gate and not physical-lab transfer.

observations.mechanism: trust-guarded scientific memory and tailored context views are useful implementation patterns, but current AutoSci evaluation does not isolate their causal contribution
observations.evidence: AutoSci records failed attempts and unresolved limitations into structured memory, routes all memory writes through a Trust Guard with deterministic form checks plus independent content review, quarantines Block writes, and supplies each skill a tailored SciMem view instead of the entire memory graph. However, its two case studies explicitly state that the goal is not to test an isolated skill and both use the full system, so this is supporting architecture evidence rather than a matched memory-gate ablation.
observations.scope: End-to-end computational research case studies. Supports inspectable memory-write and context-selection patterns; does not establish causal benefit of Trust Guard or relevance/revalidation by itself.

inferences.proposal: Separate two questions in scientist memory: whether a failure-derived record deserves to exist, and whether it is qualified for the current target. EvoScientist's IVE ablation supports the first; the Negative Knowledge transfer counterexample still motivates the second.

A record may claim domain_general only as metadata. Bypassing target revalidation requires an independently prequalified current curator digest; otherwise the receiver must perform the same mechanism-assumption and target-probe checks required for cross-domain transfer.

A revalidation check marked pass is not sufficient by itself: the referenced evidence digest must be available in the receiving context and must not be contradicted or superseded. Curator-record freshness is independently bound by record_id to the current curator digest.
